title: A Survey of Time Series Data Forecasting Methods Based on Deep Learning
authors: Chen, J.; Chen, T.; Wang, Y.; Wang, L.
venue: Journal of Basic and Applied Research International
tldr: This survey reviews deep learning architectures for time series forecasting, comparing CNNs, RNNs, LSTMs, GRUs, and Transformers across evaluation metrics including MAE, MSE, and R-squared.
problem_and_motivation: Traditional machine learning approaches struggle to handle massive time series datasets generated by IoT sensors due to their inability to capture complex temporal dependencies. Deep learning methods have shown significant progress but a comprehensive comparative evaluation across architectures using standardized benchmarks remains needed.
approach: Conducted a comprehensive literature review of deep learning-based time series forecasting methods including CNNs, RNNs, LSTMs, GRUs, and Transformers.
Performed prediction experiments using the ETT (Electricity Transformer Temperature) dataset with multiple subsets at different sampling intervals.
Evaluated models using standardized metrics: MSE, RMSE, MAE, MAPE, SMAPE, and R-squared.
Compared architectural strengths and weaknesses of RNN-based models versus Transformer-based models for sequential data processing.
Analyzed the evolution from simple RNNs to gated variants (LSTM, GRU) and self-attention-based Transformers.
findings: LSTM networks effectively address vanishing gradient problems in standard RNNs through their gating mechanisms (forget gate, input gate, output gate).
GRUs achieve similar or better performance than LSTMs with fewer parameters due to simplified gating.
Transformer self-attention mechanisms capture long-range dependencies more effectively than RNNs but suffer quadratic complexity.
Autoformer introduced deep decomposition architecture integrating time series decomposition into Transformers for the first time.
RNN models excel at capturing long-term dependencies while Transformers are more efficient with parallel computation.
The choice of evaluation metric depends on model characteristics: RNN models emphasize structure modeling while Transformers emphasize predictive accuracy.

definitions.definition: Convolutional Neural Network, a deep learning architecture that applies convolutional filters to extract spatial features.
Recurrent Neural Network, a neural network with loops allowing information persistence across timesteps.
Long Short-Term Memory, an RNN variant with gating mechanisms to handle long-range dependencies and vanishing gradients.
Gated Recurrent Unit, a simplified LSTM variant with update and reset gates for efficient sequence modeling.
A neural network architecture based on self-attention mechanisms that processes sequences in parallel.
Electricity Transformer Temperature dataset used for evaluating time series forecasting models.
Mean Absolute Error, the average absolute difference between predicted and actual values.
Mean Squared Error, the average squared difference between predicted and actual values.
Root Mean Squared Error, the square root of MSE emphasizing larger errors.
Mean Absolute Percentage Error, measuring relative magnitude of prediction errors.
Symmetric Mean Absolute Percentage Error, a modification of MAPE avoiding large values when actuals are small.
Coefficient of Determination measuring the proportion of variance explained by the model.

topics.name: Forecasting Algorithms for Sequential Spending Data
topics.justification: Directly reviews forecasting algorithms including LSTM, GRU, and Transformers for sequential time series data.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This survey provides a comprehensive review and comparison of deep learning architectures for time series forecasting, covering CNNs, RNNs, LSTMs, GRUs, and Transformers. It systematically evaluates these models using the ETT dataset and standard metrics, highlighting the strengths and weaknesses of each approach. The paper establishes foundational knowledge for selecting appropriate deep learning methods for time series prediction tasks across various domains.
directly_justifies: LSTM networks effectively address vanishing gradient problems through gating mechanisms for sequential data.
GRUs achieve comparable performance to LSTMs with fewer parameters and higher computational efficiency.
Transformer self-attention mechanisms capture long-range dependencies more effectively than recurrent architectures.
The choice between RNN and Transformer models depends on whether structure modeling or predictive accuracy is prioritized.
limits: The survey focuses primarily on deep learning methods without extensive comparison with traditional statistical approaches.
Experimental evaluation is limited to the ETT dataset, which may not generalize across all time series domains.
The paper does not address real-world deployment challenges or computational cost trade-offs.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: A systematic scan of all topic domains was conducted. Domain 6 (Predictive Modeling) was flagged as highly relevant because the paper directly reviews forecasting algorithms for sequential data. No other topic domains from the taxonomy were applicable, as the paper is a pure technical survey of deep learning architectures without personal finance, budgeting, or behavioral dimensions.

limitations: Limited to the ETT dataset for experimental evaluation, which may not represent all time series characteristics.
Does not compare deep learning methods with traditional statistical forecasting models in a unified framework.
Computational cost and deployment considerations are not systematically addressed.
remember_this: LSTM gating mechanisms solve the vanishing gradient problem in standard RNNs for long sequences.
GRUs offer similar performance to LSTMs with fewer parameters and higher efficiency.
Transformer self-attention outperforms RNNs for long-range dependency capture but with quadratic complexity.
The Autoformer integrates time series decomposition directly into the Transformer architecture.
